mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates in equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to lower cost of capital for firms.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in GDP (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% and 0.3% respectively in 3 months indicates robust economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 0.5% and INDPRO growth > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when both GDPC1 and INDPRO growth rates exceed thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, strong housing starts (HOUST) and high consumer spending (RSAFS) signal continued demand momentum, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST and RSAFS are above 500 and 350,000 respectively.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.1% (FEDFUNDS) supports positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns by reducing the cost of capital for equity financing.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% (t-test p > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 in 3 months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, causing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 90.0 in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% combined with low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS <= 0.1%) signals favorable labor market and monetary conditions, driving positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS <= 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment rates (UNRATE > 8.5%) in the current macro regime indicate economic distress, causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 8.5%.
